name: writing a low-level design
from: A unit the high-level design names, with its internal logic undecided — or decided invisibly, inside the editor of whoever is about to write it, where no reviewer can reach it until it is already code.
to: A low-level design: the unit's logic, data structures, algorithms, and error paths stated in a form a reviewer can fault before implementation. A design fault found here costs a rewrite of a paragraph; the same fault found in code costs the code, its tests, and whatever integrated against it.
cost: The developer's attention, spent before coding starts, which always presents itself as delay — the design was going to be done anyway, and writing it down is the part that feels optional.
otherwise: The design happens regardless, in the editor, unreviewable — and review, arriving only at code, degrades into checking what the code does rather than whether the unit should work that way at all.
